item.title: Analytical Modeling of the Admittance Tensor of Periodic Elliptical Meta-Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A metasurface is an electrically thin interface that controls the phase, amplitude and polarization of a wave, upon reflection or transmission. Printed on a grounded dielectric substrate and spatially modulated across the aperture, it converts a guided surface wave into a radiated leaky wave, a mechanism used in holographic metasurface antennas. Controlling this conversion requires synthesizing a prescribed distribution of admittance tensors, each derived from the homogenization of a subwavelength unit cell. Many numerical and semi-analytical methods have been proposed to relate the geometry of a meta-atom to the tensor it produces. This paper presents, to the author's knowledge, the first analytical model, restricted to elliptical meta-atoms on a uniform lattice. The Galerkin method is applied directly to the geometry of the patches, without spatial meshing. An affine transformation maps any rotated ellipse onto the unit disk, so that a single formulation covers every configuration. A wideband response takes from minutes to tens of minutes with a periodic full-wave solver, while the proposed model evaluates it in a few tens of milliseconds on the same workstation, roughly three orders of magnitude faster. The predicted admittance agrees with a method-of-moments reference up to the fundamental resonance and captures the guided-mode anomaly of the substrate. Beyond the physical insight it brings, the model is a differentiable function of the geometry, which makes the quasi-real-time design of optimized metasurfaces possible.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Froment\`eze

item.title: Localized oscillations of an Euler--Bernoulli beam with time-varying parameters on a visco-elastic foundation: asymptotics, adiabatic invariant, and equivalent Hamiltonian system
item.description: arXiv:2606.22444v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider localized oscillations of an Euler--Bernoulli beam on a visco-elastic foundation coupled to a damped discrete oscillator. All system parameters vary slowly and independently in time. For the conservative case, we employ three different analytical approaches: an asymptotic method, a technique based on the adiabatic invariance of the action of a trapped wave, and an analysis of the equivalent Hamiltonian system. All three approaches yield the identical formula for the oscillation amplitude. In the dissipative case, the oscillation amplitude is obtained solely via the asymptotic approach. Finally, we validate our analytical findings against numerical simulations, demonstrating excellent agreement.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina V. Shishkina, Serge N. Gavrilov, Yulia A. Mochalova
